thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Tumbles 400 Points as Italian Spark Starts Market Fire

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Tumbles 400 Points as Italian Spark Starts Market Fire
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 29, 2018 2:00 p.m. ET The Dow Jones Industrial Average is slumping today as what happens in Italy doesn't stay in Italy. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...look at the issues beyond Italy contributing to today's market selloff;
•...explain why Kinder Morgan (KMI) is rallying;
•...and highlight Walt Disney's (DIS) double dose of headline fodder.
That Escalated Quickly A new report says U.S. consumers are more confident today than they have been at any time since before 9/11. Yes, really.
But it's not helping stocks.
Why not? Blame the Italians, whose latest political drama is once again sending tremors through the entire global financial system.
You might also blame President Donald Trump's decision to ramp the trade spat with China back up. He said he's planning to impose tariffs on $50 billion in imports and restrict some Chinese investment in U.S. companies. Of course, this is only what he's saying now. Tomorrow, as someone once said, is another day.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell some 400 points by late morning, while the S&P 500 was off 1.25% and the Russell 2000 small-cap index fell 0.87%.
Across the NYSE and Nasdaq, falling stocks outnumbered rising ones by about 2-3.
Oil fell another $1.35 to around $66.50 on growing hopes—or fears, depending on how you're affected—that OPEC is going to increase production.
Illustration: Bloomberg News Italian fears are already hammering the stocks of major banks exposed to the eurozone's third-biggest economy. Deutsche Bank (DB) stock is in freefall, tumbling another 6% on debt fears. George Soros was out helping the mood by spreading more doom and gloom about another financial crisis.
Isn’t gold supposed to go up at moments like this? The precious metal went nowhere.
New data out from the Conference Board says U.S. consumers' confidence about the present situation jumped this month to its highest reading since March 2001.
Apple (AAPL) was off nearly 0.7%, despite an unconfirmed report that the OLED screen currently used only on the flagship iPhone X will in future be standard on all new iPhones. Tesla (TSLA) jumped another 1%. It's been looking pretty good since the middle of last week, when head honcho Elon Musk jumped on the Lugenpresse bandwagon and began denouncing "the media." Facebook (FB) was slammed with the devastating news that it is being banned for a month in Papua New Guinea over fake-news issues. The stock, somehow, just about kept its head above water.
S&P 500 : -1.4% to 2683.31
Dow 30 : -421.95 points, or -1.7%, to 24,331.14
Nasdaq : -0.9% to 7367.51
Vix : +23.9% to 16.38
10-year Treasury Yield : -0.11 percentage point to 2.82%
Midday Movers Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) is down 3% to $158.45 after naming Nathanial Dalton as its new CEO , as its former chief executive Sean Healey is stepping down after being diagnosed with ALS.
Illustration: Getty Images Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) is up 4.3% to $43.59 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The consulting company earned 52 cents a share on revenue of $1.4 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 46 cents a share on revenue of $1.67 billion.
Kinder Morgan (KMI) is up 3% to $16.35 on reports that Canada plans to buy its Trans Mountain Pipeline project.
Quest Diagnostics (DGX) is up 0.5% to $106.31 after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to Overweight. Analyst Ricky Goldwasser boosted her rating on the stock to Overweight, with a $192 price target, following news of a partnership with UnitedHealth Group (UNH) announced last week.
Walt Disney (DIS) is down 2.1% to $100.05 on a report from CNBC that it is lining up additional financing if Comcast (CMCSA) gives 21st Century Fox (FOXA) a superior offer. Oh, and Solo: A Star Wars Story disappointed , too. Comcast is off 0.8% at $31.49, while 21st Century Fox has fallen 1% to $38.65. — Teresa Rivas
